title: NaxRiscv (SpinalHDL/NaxRiscv)
_note: NaxRiscv is SpinalHDL's out-of-order superscalar RV32 core: `sbt runMain
naxriscv.Gen` elaborates the default configuration -- 2 ALUs, 2-wide decode,
an LSU2 load / store unit with 16-entry LQ and SQ, MMU, branch prediction,
perf counters, M + S + U -- into ONE NaxRiscv.v holding the core and its 23
submodules: the data cache, the issue queue and its dependency storage, the
multi-port register files and their multi-write RAMs (the
RamAsyncMwXor / RamAsyncMwMux families, from the MultiPortWritesSymplifier
transformation phase), the radix-4 divider, the MMU translator and the
stream FIFOs.  24 rows.
test/ext_ip/naxriscv_setup.sh runs the generation.  Unlike VexRiscv, the
build takes SpinalHDL FROM SOURCE -- build.sbt sets
`val spinalVersion = "dev"` and reaches core / lib / sim / idslplugin
through `ProjectRef(file("ext/SpinalHDL"), ...)` -- so the SpinalHDL
submodule is a build input, not a resolved artifact, and ext/rvls has to be
cloned too because `Compile / unmanagedSourceDirectories` puts its JNI
bindings on the Scala source path.  The other two submodules (NaxSoftware,
riscv-isa-sim) are simulation-only and are NOT cloned: NaxSoftware alone is
several GB of pre-built test binaries.
The generation also writes NaxRiscvSynt.v, which is NOT a root: it is the
same 24 modules wrapped for area benchmarking (`Rtl.xorOutputs(Rtl.ffIo(c))`
registers and XOR-reduces every port, so the wrapper's logic is not the
core's), and compiling both would duplicate every module name.
First local sweep 2026-10-28: 24 / 24 elaborate, 17 / 24 proven, 24 / 24
co-sim PASS, 24 / 24 with 0 undriven, 0 `read_uhdm` divergences, 0 `differs`
and no read-fails -- the family landed with no open reader lead.  The 7
unproven rows are all SAT budget on datapaths this miter depth cannot close:
DataCache and the NaxRiscv top go over the memory cap, and DependencyStorage,
RamAsyncMwMux_3, RamAsyncMwXor_11, RegFileAsync and TranslatorWithRollback
time out at 300 s.
Two co-sim rows are weak by construction and the numbers say so:
PrefetchPredictor reports 0 ACTIVE cycles because prefetching is off in this
configuration and SpinalHDL emits it as a stub (`io_prediction_cmd_valid =
1'b0`, payload all-X), and the NaxRiscv top reports 1, because nothing in the
core moves until its instruction and data buses are answered and random
stimulus never does.  Neither is evidence of anything; the formal column is
the real check on those two.
